amrex::DistributionMapping dm_full_domain
 the DistributionMapping every full-domain multifab is built on. Each of those covers the domain in a single box, so the map holds one entry, and which rank it names is whichever holds the least fab memory when it is built. Building one per allocator therefore put the mask and the data it weights on different ranks under MPI. Empty until full_domain_dmap first needs it.

 Source of the biology tracer initial condition, independent of remora.ic_type. Default follows ic_type.
 
int use_biology_cpp_answer = 1
 Select the native C++ biology kernel (1) or the ROMS Fortran bridge oracle (0). Only meaningful when built with USE_FENNEL_FORT=TRUE; ignored otherwise. Runtime-controlled so the two paths can be compared without a rebuild.
 
int biology_debug = 0
 Biology diagnostic verbosity: 0 off, 1 target column, 2 all columns. See Source/Biology/Fortran/tag_map.md.
 
int biology_debug_i = 2
 Target column i index for biology_debug = 1.
 
int biology_debug_j = 2
 Target column j index for biology_debug = 1.
 
int nfast
 Number of fast steps to take.
 
int do_substep = 1
 Whether to substep fine levels in time.
 
bool time_interp_flux = false
 interpolate the parent's barotropic mass flux in time at the coarse-fine interface, rather than holding its step average. Off matches most ROMS configurations.
 
int cf_impose_flux = 0
 impose the parent's barotropic mass flux on DUon/DVom at the coarse-fine interface, rather than relying on the velocity written by set_2d_cf_bcs being turned back into the same flux. Off by default: it improves conservation but does not cure the two-level barotropic instability seen in Channel_Test.
 
int do_reflux = 1
 correct the coarse tracer with the finer level's accumulated advective flux at their interface. Only has an effect under remora.do_substep with two-way coupling.
 
int cf_avgdown_perimeter = 1
 exclude the coarse-fine perimeter's normal-velocity faces from the fine-to-coarse average, as ROMS does. 1 (default) matches ROMS; 0 restores the old behaviour.
 
int cf_fill_vel_after = 0
 re-fill the child's 3D velocity from the parent after the step, so the coarse-fine boundary carries the parent's shear profile rather than the one vert_mean_3d left there. Diagnostic; off, so it changes no answer unless set. Both drivers do it only under this knob – see the comment in Advance. On the ratio-3 Dogbone it moves level-1 x-velocity by 4.1e-3 relative and level 0 by 1.9e-4 after 20 steps.
 
int cf_set_2d_bcs = 1
 0 = never impose the 2D coarse-fine interface condition, 1 = every fast step, 2 = only the first fast step of each baroclinic step.
 
int cf_avgdown_bar = 1
 
int cf_fill_all_kcomp = 1
 write every leapfrog record of the coarse-fine ghost band, as put_refine2d does when it sets zeta(:,:,1:3) and Zt_avg1 to one value; without it those records go a whole parent step stale. On by default. Roundoff on the ROMS-matched deck, where the fine zeta halo is barely read, but the dominant cost to volume conservation on the subcycled dogbone: 2.0e-09 to 2.9e-08 of drift over 20 steps, volume being the integral of the free surface this writes. ROMS makes the same trade.
 
int cf_time_interp_zeta = 1
 interpolate the parent in time onto the child's own sub-time, as put_refine2d does, rather than freezing it at the end of the parent step. On by default, and non-conservative for the same reason as cf_fill_all_kcomp: 1.4e-08 of volume drift on its own.
 
int cf_flux_pc = 1
 distribute the parent's interface mass flux piecewise-constantly over the fine faces under each parent face, as ROMS's get_persisted2d does, instead of with the linear tangential variation of AMReX's face interpolator. Both conserve the total; they differ in the profile along the interface. On by default: it removes the fine level's own excess divergence there.
 
int cf_avgdown_stencil = 1
 average the fine velocity onto the coarse over ROMS's nine-point stencil (fine2coarse2d, half-width (Rscale-1)/2 in both directions) instead of only the faces that tile the coarse face. On by default: with cf_flux_pc it takes the interface refinement perturbation from 1.29x ROMS's to 1.01x on the matched dogbone, the residual 1% closing only with cf_impose_flux, which stays off. Not conservative in principle – the nine-point mean does not preserve transport across the interface – but only about 3e-10 of volume drift in practice, well under the free-surface ghost band's cost.
 
int cf_avgdown_volume_weighted = 0
 average the fine tracers onto the coarse weighted by cell volume, Hz/(pm*pn), rather than by area as ROMS's fine2coarse3d does. Off by default. Where the fine layer thickness varies under a coarse cell, as interpolated bathymetry near land makes it, the area mean gains or loses tracer content. Volume weighting keeps it only where the coarse cell's volume matches the fine volumes under it, so not at a coast, and it is not applied to the initial high-resolution cascade (average_down_with_grow_cells).
 
int cf_print_iface = -1
 print the imposed coarse-fine interface velocity at this baroclinic step (-1 = off). Diagnostic only; the fine level is not in the NetCDF output.
 
int reflux_clamp = 1
 stop that correction driving a tracer negative, as ROMS does. On by default to match ROMS; costs exact conservation on any step that clamps.
 
int check_cf_metrics_flag = 0
 measure whether fine cell edges tile the coarse ones at a coarse-fine interface, which is what makes the imposed mass flux conservative

Receives atmospheric flux lanes from the driver and assembles REMORA flux inputs.

Expected active-lane order matches the driver FluxPassing contract: tau_x, tau_y, SHflux, LHflux, SWrad, LWrad, rain, evap.

◆ average_down_with_grow_cells()

void REMORA::average_down_with_grow_cells ( int  lev,
amrex::Vector< std::unique_ptr< amrex::MultiFab > > &  mf,
bool  use_mask = false 
)

Average down from level lev+1 to lev in mf, including grow cells.

Average a full-domain field from crse_lev+1 onto crse_lev, grow cells included.

With use_mask this takes REMORAMaskedAvgDown's mask-weighted mean instead of the plain one, so the initial state on a coarse cell only partly covered by water comes from that water. It is the formula AverageDownTo applies every step, so the initial and the running state agree on what a land point holds – unless cf_avgdown_volume_weighted is set, which this cascade ignores for want of a full-domain Hz. A two-way run then averages down once before its first step, so only the coarse cells outside the fine grids keep the area mean. Leave use_mask off for grid metrics: a cell size is well defined under land, and masking pm/pn would corrupt it.

Parameters
[in]crse_levlevel to average data down to
[in,out]vec_mfvector over levels of multifabs containing data to average

"True" vertical velocity w (m/s) at w-points, as ROMS wvelocity

The "true" vertical velocity w (m/s) at w-points, a port of ROMS wvelocity. In terrain-following coordinates 

Hz * omega = w - d(z)/d(t) - div(z),   div(z) = pm * u * d(z)/d(xi) + pn * v * d(z)/d(eta)

so w adds back to omega the stretching of the levels by the moving free surface (from the barotropic flux divergence) and the motion along the sloping levels, which is computed at rho-points and shifted to w-points with ROMS's cubic interpolation. ◆ estTimeStep()

Real REMORA::estTimeStep ( int  level) const

compute dt from CFL considerations

Estimate the largest stable slow (baroclinic) timestep on a level.

The estimate is the smaller of an advective limit and an external gravity wave limit, each a maximum over the wet cells of the level: 

dt_adv  = cfl / max( |u|*pm, |v|*pn, |w|/Hz )
dt_grav = cfl * ndtfast / max( sqrt(g*|h|) * sqrt(pm^2 + pn^2) )

The second is the Courant quantity ROMS forms as Cg_max in metrics.F. It is what keeps the estimate finite for a run started from rest, where every velocity is zero and the advective limit alone is undefined.

pm and pn are the per-cell 1/dx and 1/dy metric terms rather than the geometry's uniform cell size, so stretched and curvilinear grids give the right answer.

Parameters
[in]levellevel of refinement

◆ init_biology_ic()

void REMORA::init_biology_ic ( int  lev)

Initialize biology tracers from whichever source remora.biology_ic_type selects. Call after the physical fields exist: the analytic profiles are functions of temperature.

Initialize the biology tracers from whichever source remora.biology_ic_type selects.

Deliberately decoupled from remora.ic_type. A NetCDF initial file supplies only the tracers it happens to contain – the BioToy file has oxygen but no PO4 or ODU – so validating an option set the file does not cover would otherwise mean regenerating binary input that no fresh clone can reproduce. With biology_ic_type = analytic the physical fields still come from NetCDF while biology comes from the problem's analytic profile.

Must be called after the physical fields are initialized: the analytic biology profiles are functions of temperature.

[in]levlevel to initialize on

◆ init_full_domain_from_analytic()

void REMORA::init_full_domain_from_analytic ( )

Initialize high-resolution initial data, zeta included, from analytic functions.

Evaluate the analytic initial state, free surface, and biology on the full domain at hires_init_level and average them down to level 0.

That level does not exist yet, so its coordinates are built here: x_r and y_r from the cell size (constant grid scale), z_r and z_w from the free surface and the bathymetry. ◆ inject_mask_outside_domain()

void REMORA::inject_mask_outside_domain ( int  lev)

Give lev's rho-mask ghost cells beyond the domain the coarser level's values.

Overwrite lev's rho-mask ghost cells beyond the domain edge with the coarser level's mask there, injected piecewise-constant.

FillCoarsePatchPC fills those cells with foextrap, which copies the interior outward, even across a periodic edge. At a river mouth on a wall that turns the land behind the river wet, and the clamped boundary's salt then mixes into the river cell; at a periodic edge it ignores whatever lies across the seam. Level 0 takes these cells from its grid file, or from a periodic FillBoundary, so the coarser level's ghost cells hold the right mask.

Parameters
[in]levlevel to operate on, > 0

roll a two-snapshot history of a level's end-of-step 2D state

Roll a two-snapshot history of one level's end-of-step 2D state: the previous "new" becomes "old" and src becomes the new one, so the pair brackets [t_old, t_new] of the step just taken. src has one component and is broadcast to all of them. On the first call, and whenever the level's layout changes, both snapshots are set to src, making the child's time interpolation a no-op for that step rather than reading uninitialised data – the same special case ROMS takes when RollingIndex is still zero.

◆ set_2d_cf_bcs()

void REMORA::set_2d_cf_bcs ( int  lev,
amrex::Real  time,
int  know,
int  knew 
)

set this level's barotropic contact points from its parent, mass-conservingly

Set the normal barotropic velocity on this level's coarse-fine interface from the parent's time-averaged mass flux, as ROMS does in put_refine2d (nesting.F): 

ubar_f = Dubar_c / D_f,    D_f = 0.5*(h + zeta)_{i-1} + 0.5*(h + zeta)_i

D comes from know; ROMS instead uses one time index for both sides: u2dbc_im.F's nested branch builds D from zeta(kout) and writes ubar(kout), and put_refine2d uses indx1 for both. Since the next half-step forms DUon = ubar(krhs)*D(krhs) with krhs equal to this knew, ROMS recovers Dubar_parent exactly while this carries an extra D(knew)/D(know). Measured at most 1.2e-07 on the step-1 Channel_Test interface velocity, against a 2.4e-03 artifact, with no change to Dogbone volume drift or the Channel_Test blow-up.

Momentum only. setup_step resets all three zeta components to Zt_avg1, so what a finer level interpolates for the free surface is already the parent's fast-time average – as in ROMS, where set_zeta runs ahead of put_refine2d.

Parameters
[in]levlevel of refinement
[in]timesimulation time to interpolate the parent's flux to
[in]knowzeta time component to take the sea surface height from
[in]knewubar/vbar time component to set

◆ cf_avgdown_stencil

int REMORA::cf_avgdown_stencil = 1
private

average the fine velocity onto the coarse over ROMS's nine-point stencil (fine2coarse2d, half-width (Rscale-1)/2 in both directions) instead of only the faces that tile the coarse face. On by default: with cf_flux_pc it takes the interface refinement perturbation from 1.29x ROMS's to 1.01x on the matched dogbone, the residual 1% closing only with cf_impose_flux, which stays off. Not conservative in principle – the nine-point mean does not preserve transport across the interface – but only about 3e-10 of volume drift in practice, well under the free-surface ghost band's cost.

◆ cf_avgdown_volume_weighted

int REMORA::cf_avgdown_volume_weighted = 0
private

average the fine tracers onto the coarse weighted by cell volume, Hz/(pm*pn), rather than by area as ROMS's fine2coarse3d does. Off by default. Where the fine layer thickness varies under a coarse cell, as interpolated bathymetry near land makes it, the area mean gains or loses tracer content. Volume weighting keeps it only where the coarse cell's volume matches the fine volumes under it, so not at a coast, and it is not applied to the initial high-resolution cascade (average_down_with_grow_cells).

◆ cf_fill_all_kcomp

int REMORA::cf_fill_all_kcomp = 1
private

write every leapfrog record of the coarse-fine ghost band, as put_refine2d does when it sets zeta(:,:,1:3) and Zt_avg1 to one value; without it those records go a whole parent step stale. On by default. Roundoff on the ROMS-matched deck, where the fine zeta halo is barely read, but the dominant cost to volume conservation on the subcycled dogbone: 2.0e-09 to 2.9e-08 of drift over 20 steps, volume being the integral of the free surface this writes. ROMS makes the same trade.

◆ t_new

amrex::Vector<amrex::Real> REMORA::t_new
private

new time at each level, in seconds since start_time

Model time is split into a double start_time and a Real elapsed time, as ROMS splits DSTART from the time it advances. The solver, the FillPatch time interpolation, and the kernels only ever see elapsed time, which stays small enough for a float to resolve a timestep. Anything that needs a time on the model clock – forcing and boundary files, the calendar, output time stamps, user-given times – goes through model_time() in double.
